questions.feedback: If you picked carbon dioxide, that is the trap: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide. Reteach point: The released oxygen comes from water: splitting water gives the oxygen, while carbon dioxide supplies the carbon for glucose.
questions.misconception: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide.
questions.prompt: Where does the oxygen released in photosynthesis come from?

questions.answer: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen (with light energy trapped by chlorophyll)
questions.feedback: A strong answer has carbon dioxide and water on the left, glucose and oxygen on the right, and light energy powering the change. If you placed oxygen among the inputs, swap it to the product side.
questions.prompt: Write the word equation for photosynthesis.

choices.text: Through tiny pores on the underside of the leaf
Through the roots, dissolved in water
Through the stem, from the soil
It is made inside the leaf by chlorophyll

questions.feedback: Carbon dioxide enters from the air through tiny pores under the leaf. Water is the input that arrives from the roots - keep the two entry routes separate.
questions.prompt: How does carbon dioxide enter a leaf?

questions.answer: Photosynthesis needs light energy, trapped by chlorophyll, to power the building of glucose. In darkness there is no light energy, so the change cannot run and no new glucose is made, even with both raw materials present.
questions.feedback: The missing ingredient is the energy input: light. Carbon dioxide and water are materials, but without light energy trapped by chlorophyll there is nothing to power the building of glucose.
questions.prompt: A plant is kept in complete darkness for two days. Explain why it stops making glucose, even though carbon dioxide and water are still available.
